newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas grounds Explorer copters.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas grounds Explorer copters.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas on Thursday said it grounded its MD Explorer helicopters after the discovery of a broken adjustable collective drive link, which is a component of the rotor head system.

McDonnell Douglas said it contacted all operators of the 31 delivered helicopters instructing them not to fly the aircraft until further notice. It also said it notified the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) of its action.
A spokesman said the company had not determined when the helicopters would be back in operation. "We're testing them. It could be tomorrow or as long as a month," he said.
The spokesman said the company did not expect the action to have an impact on its financial results.
The company said the MD Explorer has been accident-free since entering service 2-1/2 years ago.
The part is made by Phoenix-based Houston and Waller.

McDonnell Douglas said it first discovered a problem during a post-flight inspection on May 8. It notified operators May 9 and began investigating and testing the drive link to determine the cause. It sent operators replacement link assemblies with instructions to replace the part.
Subsequent laboratory tests revealed that the drive link assembly requires redesign.
The company said a second, dual-path, fixed-link assembly continued to function in the May 8 incident and was not affected by the action.
